feed.rights: Explanations and summaries are generated by AI from the original text. Dates, rates and amounts are checked against the source, but errors are still possible, so always rely on the original. Nothing here is legal, tax or investment advice.

entry.title: Stealth addresses after secp256k1 breaks: payer clawback and signature-derived keys
entry.summary: Stealth addresses after secp256k1 falls: payer clawback, signature-derived keys, and a recovery statement for ERC-8441 outputs ethresear.ch · Nov 27, 2026This Ethereum Research forum post examines the security of stealth addresses under ERC-5564 scheme 1 and ERC-8441 scheme 3 if secp256k1 is broken by a quantum adversary. The author argues that scheme 1 leaves unspent outputs fully exposed, while scheme 3 restores hash-based protection for unspent outputs. Remaining gaps include payer clawback, future spending rights granted to scanners, and signature-derived keys that undermine the ML-KEM layer.

entry.title: A state-backed test of SETCODEFROM and two proposed rules
entry.summary: A state-backed validation of SETCODEFROM ethresear.ch · Nov 27, 2026The authors tested the draft of EIP-8298, which adds a SETCODEFROM instruction, against Ethereum mainnet bytecode. They found that it lets an account show one code while running another, which breaks sudoswap's router and lets borrowed code replace a Safe's proxy. They propose two rules: record the new code hash and switch only when the outermost frame ends, and allow an account's code to be replaced only by its own code.

entry.title: Paths to post-quantum execution in Hegotá: an experimental comparison
entry.summary: Paths to post-quantum execution in Hegotá: an experimental comparison ethresear.ch · Nov 27, 2026This study compares four proposals for introducing post-quantum signatures in Ethereum's Hegotá fork, implemented on the ethrex execution client without aggregation (M1) and with builder-side aggregation (M2). The authors find that inline PROOF frames have the smallest implementation footprint in M1. They argue that Hegotá should offer post-quantum authorization before production-ready aggregation is available.

entry.title: A technical discussion on handling post-quantum signatures on the script stack, and how to safely process stack elements larger than 520 bytes
entry.summary: Handling PQ signatures on the stack Delving Bitcoin · Nov 27, 2026Bitcoin developers discuss how to allow script stack elements larger than 520 bytes so that post-quantum signatures such as SHRINCS can fit. The thread compares three approaches: chunking across elements, blacklisting certain opcodes, and optimizing implementations. It also weighs the trade-offs and denial-of-service risks of each.

entry.title: Wallet rebroadcast can link addresses to node IPs
entry.summary: Exploiting Wallet Rebroadcast to Link Addresses to Node IPs and More Delving Bitcoin · Nov 26, 2026This Delving Bitcoin post explains how Bitcoin Core's wallet rebroadcast behavior leaks privacy. An attacker sends a small payment to a target address and watches which node re-announces it 12 to 36 hours later, linking that address to the node's IP. In a regtest simulation the author reports correct attribution in 30 of 30 trials, and the post also covers attack cost, wallet fingerprinting, and mitigations.

entry.title: Optimal Dynamic Fees for L2s: A Vault Approach
entry.summary: Optimal Dynamic Fees for L2s: A Vault Approach ethresear.ch · Nov 25, 2026This Ethereum Research forum post summarizes a paper on how layer-2 networks should set transaction fees to recover Ethereum posting costs. It compares proportional fee rules with a linear-quadratic regulator rule that keeps part of the previous fee, trading off vault tracking against fee smoothness. The authors also show how to choose the memory coefficient and compare Arbitrum's rule with replayed historical Ethereum prices.

entry.title: A Bitcoin quantum roadmap combining BIP-361 and PACTs to protect ownership
entry.summary: A Bitcoin Quantum Roadmap: Combining BIP-361 and PACTs to Preserve Ownership Rights Delving Bitcoin · Nov 25, 2026This Delving Bitcoin forum post proposes a quantum-security roadmap that combines BIP-361 with Dan Robinson's PACT proposal. It outlines introducing quantum-resistant addresses and anonymous PACTs, freezing vulnerable legacy spending after a migration window, and allowing recovery through matured PACTs. The author suggests this approach balances quantum protection with preserving legitimate ownership rights.

entry.title: FOCIL and Ethereum's Post-Quantum Transition
entry.summary: FOCIL and Ethereum's PQ transition ethresear.ch · Nov 25, 2026This Ethereum Research forum post examines how FOCIL (fork-choice enforced inclusion lists) could evolve as Ethereum adopts post-quantum cryptography, and how the transition could affect the roles of includers, builders and attesters. It covers inclusion list committee selection, how inclusion lists can carry post-quantum transactions, and bandwidth estimates comparing inclusion lists with attestation aggregates and execution payloads.

entry.title: Knowledge-Asymmetry UTXO Rescue and Stateless Post-Quantum Threshold Signing for Legacy Bitcoin
entry.summary: 676-Byte Knowledge-Asymmetry UTXO Rescue and Stateless Lattice PQ-MPC for Legacy Supply Migration Delving Bitcoin · Nov 25, 2026The author posts on Delving Bitcoin about two techniques in the AQMP v2.0 protocol. The first rescues frozen legacy UTXOs using knowledge asymmetry from the unhardened BIP-32 parent chain code, with a total on-chain witness of 676 bytes. The second is a stateless post-quantum threshold signing engine for institutional custody, using Shamir secret sharing and HMAC-SHA3-256 synthetic nonces. The post compares witness sizes against Lifeboat and Dropkick and links to a paper and reference implementation, and the author requests technical critique of the BIP-32 chain-code assumptions and the Dual-Commit XOR mempool window bounds.

entry.title: Do bid cancellations matter? A discussion of whether proposers will respect cancelled bids under ePBS.
entry.summary: Do bid cancellations matter? ethresear.ch · Nov 24, 2026This discussion examines whether Ethereum proposers under ePBS will keep respecting bid cancellations, meaning they sign each relay's latest bid rather than the highest. The authors propose a common-value auction model and analyze header logs from the Ultrasound, Titan and bloXroute relays.

entry.title: Post-quantum data availability sampling with tighter provable security
entry.summary: Post-quantum DAS with improved provable security ethresear.ch · Nov 24, 2026This post proposes a modified version of a post-quantum DAS scheme that has a tighter provable security bound, giving a higher concrete security level but lower efficiency. The original bound contained a square-root term that weakened the security level, which the modification removes. The authors also prove the tighter bound in Lean.

entry.title: Verifying transaction inclusion against an untrusted explorer API and how much proof of work is needed
entry.summary: Checking transaction inclusion against an untrusted explorer API: how much proof of work is enough? Delving Bitcoin · Nov 24, 2026The author, who maintains btc-toolkit, a stdlib-only Python Bitcoin CLI, seeks design feedback on its verify command, which checks transactions, Merkle proofs, and block headers from an untrusted Esplora/Mempool API without a node. Headers with difficulty of at least 50 T are reported as verified, a fixed threshold the author questions as difficulty changes. The post asks whether a better anchor, checking descendant headers, or timestamp checks would strengthen the verifier.

entry.title: Bitcoin Core v31.3 Release Announcement
entry.summary: Bitcoin Core v31.3 Released Delving Bitcoin · Nov 24, 2026Bitcoin Core version 31.3 has been released with various bug fixes, performance improvements, and updated translations. Notable changes include processing only unique transaction INVs in network handling, along with several continuous integration adjustments.

entry.title: Receive screens and “expiry”: how users read payment-request expiry
entry.summary: Receive screens and 'expiry': how users read payment-request expiry Delving Bitcoin · Nov 23, 2026A wallet support staffer discusses how users interpret the expiry shown on payment requests. Many users read it as the address itself expiring, leading to fears that funds sent to an "expired" address are lost or to abandoning addresses that are still being paid. The author asks developers whether plain on-chain requests need an expiry at all and what wording makes clear that the request, not the address, has expired.

entry.title: EthCLLib: a Lean 4 framework for Ethereum consensus specs
entry.summary: EthCLLib: a Lean 4 framework for the Ethereum consensus specs ethresear.ch · Nov 23, 2026This post presents EthCLLib, a Lean 4 framework that writes the Ethereum consensus specs for the Fulu, Gloas and Heze forks in one package. It explains how a fork declares its parent and records only its changes, and how generic spec bodies take different instances for the test runner and for proofs. It also describes how state transitions are written as monadic steps that follow the pyspec order.

entry.title: What a block is and how large it can get
entry.summary: What's a block, and how big can it get? ethresear.ch · Nov 22, 2026This Ethereum Research forum discussion examines the worst-case block size after the Glamsterdam upgrade. It explains that Ethereum has two byte limits, 8 MiB for the execution-layer block under EIP-7934 and 10 MiB for consensus-layer gossip messages. The author argues that gas pricing under Glamsterdam rules does not keep blocks below either limit. The post analyzes the largest blocks found, which combine zero-byte calldata with skipped EIP-7702 authorizations, and discusses implications for FOCIL.

entry.title: Multisig Session Protocol: a draft spec for secure remote multisig setup and signing, open for review
entry.summary: Multisig Session Protocol: draft spec for remote multisig setup and signing needs review Delving Bitcoin · Nov 22, 2026The author proposes a draft specification, the Multisig Session Protocol, for setting up and signing with multisig wallets remotely over a relay treated as hostile. Cosigners authenticate ephemeral keys with a short code compared out of band, each assembles the descriptor independently and compares its hash, and signers accept only PSBTs spending from a wallet both parties hold. The author requests review of the SAS commitment construction, the join mechanism, and multi-party extension.

entry.title: Open question on a hypothetical minor “slow-sliding MTP” attack that BIP 54 might introduce
entry.summary: Open Question on a hypothetical minor "slow-sliding MTP" attack introduced by BIP 54 Delving Bitcoin · Nov 21, 2026While reviewing BIP 54, the author raises a hypothetical attack in which the median-time-past (MTP) is gradually pushed away from real-world time, making a block invalid under the timestamp rules. The author notes this would require controlling over 51% of hashrate and would have limited impact. They conclude it does not change their view of BIP 54, but share it as an interesting insight.

entry.title: Node Attestation Protocol: a non-binding way for economic nodes to signal support for Bitcoin proposals
entry.summary: Node Attestation Protocol Delving Bitcoin · Nov 21, 2026This discussion proposes the Node Attestation Protocol (NAP), which lets non-mining economic nodes publish free-form key-value statements backed by cryptographic proof of control of specific UTXOs. An aggregator validates these attestations and sums them by coin value. NAP is explicitly non-binding and intended only as a human-judged signal alongside miner signaling. The post also covers its time and coin-age limits and known weaknesses around privacy and custodial coins.

entry.title: Post Quantum Recovery Framework: a discussion of how unmigrated bitcoin could be recovered if quantum computers break elliptic curve cryptography
entry.summary: Post Quantum Recovery Framework Delving Bitcoin · Nov 21, 2026The author outlines a class of recovery schemes that add extra spending conditions to existing bitcoin UTXOs to protect them from theft if elliptic curve security is broken. It distinguishes prepared schemes, which require user action before that day, from unprepared schemes, and classifies recovery secrets as accidental or essential. The post also describes the dilemma that requiring BIP32 derivation paths could make some coins unspendable, while relying on hidden pubkeys leaves other coins open to theft.

entry.title: Unrig: A prediction market protocol designed to work without liquidity providers and resist manipulation
entry.summary: Unrig: A Prediction Market Protocol That Needs No Liquidity and Can't Be Rigged ethresear.ch · Nov 21, 2026This technical discussion posted on the Ethereum Research forum proposes Unrig, a prediction market protocol built on Ethereum. It claims counterparties form naturally without liquidity provision, and that its mathematical structure makes manipulation unprofitable. The text covers risk pricing, settlement, market creation, outcome determination, and token economics.
